name: Annual Copenhagen Film Festival 2023
description:
The Annual Copenhagen Film Festival expands to three days and takes place for its 7th consecutive year with a richer and more diverse programme. 

>>3 days 
>>4 themes
>>27 short and feature independent films from around the world 

12-14 October at Husets Biograf!

#########################

The Annual Copenhagen Film Festival expands to three days and takes place for its 7th consecutive year from 12-14 October with a richer and more diverse programme. Setting our screen once again at our beloved Husets Biograf, this edition features 27 independent films that span 4 different themes touching upon gender identity, ethics, and everyday stories. 

Attracting a mixed audience of Copenhageners and the city's newcomers, the Annual Copenhagen Film Festival has become a meeting point for local and international cinephiles, filmmakers and industry experts. Taking place at the Husets Biograf since its first edition, ACFF24 returns once again at the cosy halls of the vibrant cultural centre putting independent cinema in the epicentre with a fresh programme of international shorts and feature films. 

This year, ACFF expands, and for the first time takes place for three days, aiming to highlight even more filmmakers from around the world. This year's Festival received 2900 submissions from around 360 countries worldwide. We are excited that so many talented international artists chose the Annual Copenhagen Film Festival to screen their films and to see that our community keeps widening.  

Separated into 2 screening slots per day, the programme features in total 6 different thematics. Putting humans in the epicentre, each slot examines other aspects of human dilemmas, gender and sex issues, as well as personal relationships through stories we can all identify with.

########################################

Programme 
Day 1 

Screening Slot 1: 19.30-20.40

Programme: 'Lights, Camera, Action!'
A film within a film. From time-travelling lunatic filmmakers to family members turned actors, and from the unique filmmaker-subject relationships to the ambitions of an actor hidden under a mask, this programme offers a sneak peek into the making of a film. 

▹The Chromakey Man, 13', William Samaha, Belgium, Category: Short Film, 2022		
▹A Fairy Tale, 20', Zoé Arene, France, Category: Short Film, 2021			
▹What We Make, 9', 	Alex Frecon, United States, Category: Comedy, 2023		
▹Time Traveling Through Time, 14', Ryan Ward, Canada, Category: Comedy, 2022	
▹Killing ourselves, 15', Maya Yadlin, Israel, Category: Short Film, 2022


**Break: 20.40-20.50


Screening Slot 2: 20.50-22.30
Programme: '(A)Moral?'
This programme of cinematic introspection examines the intricate web of morality and ethical dilemmas reminding us that the human conscience is a complex maze waiting to be explored. Films that leave us questioning the boundaries of right and wrong and igniting conversations about our own moral compasses.

▹Kim, 15', Brandon Danowski, United States, Category: Short Film, 2022	
▹Gardez, 17', Julian Isfort, Germany, Category: Comedy, 2023		
▹Bad Jew Good Girl, 12', Annika Chavez, United States, Category: Short Film, 2022	
▹Riten., 16', Hannah-Lisa Paul, Germany, Category: Short Film, 2022			
▹Spag Bol, 12', BRICK, United Kingdom, Category: Comedy, 2023
▹The Taster, 29', Sophia Bierend, Germany, Category: Short Film, 2022	

---------------------------------
Day 2: 'My Body, My Mind, and I'

The second day of the ACFF is dedicated to the theme ‘My Body, My Mind, and I’ featuring feature and short films that focus on society’s perception of bodies, minds and identities. 

Screening Slot 1: 19.30-21.05

Florencia Wehbe’s powerful yet sensitive feature film "Paula" opens this multifaceted film programme. The story of a teenager's struggle with body image becomes a poignant metaphor for the pervasive weight of beauty standards on all young women navigating a world obsessed with appearances.

▹Paula, 90', Florencia Wehbe, Italy, Category: Feature Film, 2022 

**Break: 21.05-21.15

Screening Slot 2: 21.15-22.50

The short film programme ‘My Body, My Mind, and I’, features 6 powerful films. An identity crisis, an exploration of memories and unhealed trauma through dance, the harassment of the female body in a public space, and the experience of pregnancy and miscarriage are presented through the stories of endearing, tormented and puzzling characters. 

▹Swollen, 18', Daniel Aranha Pedersen, Denmark, Category: Danish Film, 2023 
▹Movers, 15', Alec Goldberg, United States, Categories: Experimental, Short Documentary, 2023	
▹The Street Is Tough, 8', Panama, María Victoria Henríquez Vergara, Categories: Animated Film, Short Documentary, 2021	
▹The Pigeon of Waterloo, 15', Margaux Comte, United Kingdom, Category: Short Film, 2023	
▹A Small Circle, 14, Sofia Ose, Germany, Category: Short Documentary, Experimental, 2022	▹Neurolink, 24', Jens-Julius Grunderlund Dall, Denmark, Category: Danish Film, 2023		

--------------------

Day 3: ‘Stories of the absurd and the mundane'

One feature and 8 short films tell us ‘Stories of the absurd and the mundane’ on the third and final day of the 7th ACFF. 

Slot 1: 19.30-20.50
Katharina Woll’s impressive directorial debut ‘Everybody Wants To Be Loved’ combines physical humour and profound psychological shifts acting as a reflection of German urban society's ever-widening divisions. A delightful exploration of a woman torn between self-sacrifice and self-discovery.

▹Everybody Wants To Be Loved, 80', Katharina Woll, Germany, Category: Feature Film, 2022	

Break: 20.50-21.00

Slot 2: 21.00-22.40
The 7th ACFF completes with a tapestry of 8 indie shorts that narrate everyday life through a dazzling array of circumstances and events mirroring our own inexplicable and ridiculous world. Playful and satirical, unsettling and disheartening, these short films offer a searing commentary on current society. 

▹The End Of The World, 10', Aleksandra Podziewska, Czech Republic, Category: Student Film, 2020	
▹Off-Season, 14', Francescu Artily, France, Category: Short Film, 2023			
▹Going Well…, 4', HyeJeong Lee, Republic of Korea, Category: Animated Film, 2021	
▹The Stranger, 18', Tin Pak Lau, Canada, Category: Short Film, 2023
▹Ma Fatsh Leah, 4', 	Marion Auvin, France, Category:  Music Video, 2022	
▹Deadline, 13', Idan Gilboa, Israel, Category: Animated Film, 2023	
▹Short Stay, Long Stay, 15', Danny Carter, United Kingdom, Category: Short Film, 2023	
▹Short Draft, 23', Spyridon Papaspyrou, Greece, Category: Comedy, 2022

Award Ceremony: 22.40-23.00

-----------------------------

name: Kulturnatten 2023
description:
Glæd dig til et væld af spændende arrangementer, god stemning og en fornøjet summen i byens gader, når Kulturnatten vender tilbage den 13. oktober 2023.

Mere end 200 arrangører, herunder museer, teatre, kirker, ministerier og biblioteker, slår dørene op til arrangementer ud over det sædvanlige i aftentimerne fra kl. 18.00-00.00. Den 15. september er det endelige program klar på Kulturnattens hjemmeside. 

Det eneste, du behøver for at deltage, er et Kulturpas. Et Kulturpas giver adgang til alle Kulturnattens arrangementer og fri transport med bus, tog og Metro i Hovedstadsområdet (zone 1-99) fra kl. 16.00 til kl. 04.00. Kulturpasset koster 110 kroner. Børn under 12 år har gratis entré, når de følges med en voksen med Kulturpas.

Du kan fra den 15. september købe dit Kulturpas på Kulturnattens hjemmeside og hente det, så du har det digitalt på din telefon. Vil du hellere have et fysisk Kulturpas, kan du fra den 2. oktober købe det i alle 7-Eleven butikker i Hovedstadsområdet.

Hold øje med begivenheden, hvor vi løbende opdaterer med information.
